points: The November print will show whether the September quarter revenue hit the $14.5–15.5 billion guidance and whether management keeps the full-year fiscal 2027 $65–72 billion outlook — the long case rests on that record backlog translating into sustained top-line momentum.

Gross margin recovery is the key margin test: the company reported Q4 FY2026 GAAP gross margin of 17.5%, up from 9.9% in Q3, and the print must show that gain is holding as revenue scales rather than giving back.

The $60 billion-plus in new orders and record backlog entering fiscal 2027 are already on the books; the print should reveal shipment timing, backlog conversion, and whether revenue linearity supports the FY1 EPS consensus of $4.34 and FY2 EPS of $4.87.

Cash generation and working capital will be under scrutiny: Q4 FY2026 operating cash flow was $747 million, while reports suggest broader cash-flow questions linger, so the September-quarter cash trend and balance-sheet commentary matter for the long.

Customer diversification is the next demand driver: the company added several hundred enterprise and other customers over the past year, and the print should show whether enterprise demand can offset any hyperscaler lumpiness in AI server orders.

Valuation already embeds execution risk, with the stock at roughly 0.5x the theme median P/E and a PEG near 0.5x; the print needs to confirm earnings momentum toward the 19.5% FY1 and 12.3% FY2 growth to sustain a rerating.
AMD reports on November 4, five days before SMCI, and its datacenter/AI commentary will be a read-through for GPU supply, pricing, and AI server demand heading into SMCI’s call.
watch: September-quarter net sales within or above the $14.5–15.5 billion guidance — supports the long.
GAAP gross margin holds near or above the Q4 FY2026 17.5% level — supports the long.
Operating cash flow stays positive and improves sequentially from Q4’s $747 million — supports the long.
Non-GAAP EPS lands within or above the $1.01–$1.10 guided range — supports the long.
